transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Polaris Head of Search), Carlos Mendes (Polaris ML Infra), Jared Lin (Polaris Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Polaris is evaluating Redwood for a search POC combining vector embeddings plus lexical recall. Primary asks: scalable candidate generation, sub-200ms rerank latency at 200 QPS, private data handling and KMS integration.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros from our side, im maya, im the AE, liam is our se, he'll take the deep on infra and latency stuff.
[00:23] Anika: hi, im anika, head of search at polaris, mainly responsible for relevance, we're looking at a POC to move from pure bm25 to hybrid + rerank, want to understand how redwood fits.
[00:35] Liam: great, quick clarifying q — when you say rerank are you thinking a cross-encoder on top of ~100 candidates or something larger?
[00:44] Anika: yea, cross-encoder on 50-200 candidates, we care about P95 under 150-200ms for the rerank stage. today our bm25 cold path is fast but recall is limited.
[00:55] Carlos: our infra target is 200 QPS sustained for query volume spikes, sometimes 400 qps for peak minutes, and storage concerns — our corpus is ~1.2M docs with metadata.
[01:12] Maya: got it. high level we see two common patterns: a) use an ANN candidate generator (pinecone/milvus) for top-K then rerank with a cross-encoder hosted by redwood, or b) run embedding-based rerank end-to-end. we recommend hybrid for now.
[01:35] Anika: can redwood host the ANN index or do we need a third-party vector DB?
[01:42] Liam: currently we integrate with vector DBs (pinecone/milvus/weaviate) for production index management; for POC we can run hosted benchmarking where you push vectors to our dedicated pool for embedding/serving and we can simulate ANN recall. full managed index hosting is on roadmap but not GA.
[02:05] Jared: security question — our data contains PHI-ish fields, we need KMS, customer-managed keys and VPC peering or on-prem. what options do we have?
[02:18] Maya: we offer Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Private includes VPC and on-prem options plus KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with isolation; Hosted is fastest to start but not ideal for strict data residency.
[02:38] Anika: timeline? we want a POC in 3 weeks, results in 6 weeks and then decide.
[02:44] Liam: thats doable if you can share sample corpus + queries. For latency, important knobs: quantization on reranker model, GPU selection (A10 vs A100/H100), batching window and KV cache strategies.
[03:05] Maya: cost-wise dedicated reserved capacity tends to win for steady high QPS; hosted is fine for early POC. we'll model both.
[03:18] Anika: on dimensionality — we're evaluating 384 vs 1024 dims. storage and ANN performance differ a lot. any guidance?
[03:27] Liam: 384 dims (e.g., some L2-based models) reduces index size ~2.6x vs 1024 and ANN recall/latency is faster. But higher dims often yield better semantic separation. For your corpus size (~1.2M docs) 768 is a common sweet spot. Use productized quantization (8-bit, 4-bit) for embeddings to reduce footprint.
[03:55] Carlos: what about rerank model size? cross-encoder small like 3B vs bigger 7B — how does that impact latency at 200 QPS?
[04:07] Liam: 3B cross-encoder on A10/GPU with optimized kernels and batching can do ~6-12ms per item (per forward) but rerank latency depends on candidate count and batching. Example: 100 candidates * 6ms naive = 600ms, but we do efficient early-batch scoring and model optimizations; more practical is to use a bi-encoder candidate score then a light cross-encoder on top 20 candidates. That keeps P95 under 200ms in our experience.
[04:42] Anika: hmm so pipeline: bm25 -> ANN top 200 -> bi-encoder prune to 20 -> cross-encoder rerank?
[04:50] Liam: exactly. Or bm25 + ANN union then dedupe -> topN bi-encoder -> cross-encoder. The candidate pruning stage is critical to meet latency.
[05:02] Anika: in terms of throughput, can Redwood autoscale during spikes? we have bursts to 400QPS.
[05:10] Maya: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and burst capacity; Hosted has soft limits. For guaranteed spikes you'd want Dedicated with reserved bursting config and canary fallbacks to cheaper models.
[05:25] Carlos: are there any benchmarks we can see? like REDWOOD dedicated latency numbers for cross-encoder at different GPU types?
[05:33] Liam: we have internal perf profiles and can share a benchmark doc. rough numbers: 3B cross-encoder on A10 with batching and quantization gives about X tail depending on candidate pruning — we'll send concrete spreadsheets. (note: speaker mumble transcribed: "gonna send a spreadsheet with numbers and a caveat about sequence length")
[05:55] Anika: how do you handle embedding updates? our index is updated daily with new docs, and we need near real-time for some flows.
[06:04] Liam: embeddings can be incrementally upserted; we support async batching and near-real-time pipelines. For heavy write workloads we recommend Dedicated to separate write stall effects from serving.
[06:20] Jared: security again — audit logs, retention, who sees tokens? also GDPR concerns.
[06:27] Maya: Private deployment gives you a customer-managed control plane and full audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS option. For Hosted we have SOC 2 and encryption at rest but not customer-managed KMS by default.
[06:45] Anika: what's the rough TCO per month for dedicated for our targets (200 QPS sustained, 1.2M docs, 5k new docs/day)?
[06:55] Maya: we'll model that and return a tailored quote — it's an action item. But directionally, dedicated is often 30-50% cheaper per-token for sustained workloads due to reserved capacity.
[07:07] Carlos: about vector DBs — we currently run Milvus on k8s and evaluate Pinecone; any pitfalls integrating Redwood?
[07:15] Liam: typical integration is straightforward: Redwood serves embeddings + reranker and calls out to your Milvus cluster via SDK for ANN; we support hybrid search where we union results from BM25/Elastic and ANN. For managed cases we provide integration docs and example code. Note: sometimes naming conflicts in metadata fields require small ETL mapping — common in our setups.
[07:40] Anika: latency budget: user perceivable needs 300ms end-to-end; can we achieve that with hybrid and cross-encoder?
[07:47] Liam: yes, with candidate pruning and using bi-encoder for most scoring we can hit ~200-300ms E2E P95. Cross-encoder on full 200 is tough.
[07:59] Maya: question from sales ops — who are the stakeholders for security sign-off?
[08:05] Jared: thats me + legal + info-sec. we'll need SOC 2 docs and an architecture diagram.
[08:12] Maya: we'll share the security pack.
[08:16] (short crosstalk)
[08:24] [Recording skips briefly; transcription picks up]
[08:42] Anika: are function calls or structured output relevant here? we were thinking of extracting facets from reranked responses for UI.
[08:52] Liam: we support structured outputs and function-like responses; for rerank you'd generally return IDs + scores and then call a separate microservice to fetch document fields and facet extraction — or run a lightweight extraction model post-rerank.
[09:08] Carlos: any demo or POC template?
[09:12] Maya: yes we'll send a POC runbook: sample infra diagrams, steps to upload sample data, suggested models, metrics to capture (recall@k, MRR, latency P95), and an ops checklist for switching to Dedicated/Private.
[09:28] Anika: ok good. on embeddings model choice — we've been using a household open model at 768 dims. curious if Redwood recommends specific encoder families?
[09:38] Liam: we surface model profiles in the catalog; for search we usually recommend models tuned for semantic similarity with >>> stable embeddings; if you need smaller dims we can recommend a 384/768 family. We also suggest experimenting with whitening and L2 norming for hybrid scores.
[09:55] Anika: how does Redwood handle cold-cache startup? we worry about KV cache misses for long sessions.
[10:02] Liam: runtime uses prefix/KV cache to warm contexts; for search rerank it's less about KV cache and more about model weights; we do fast cold starts with warmed instances or prewarmed pools for dedicated sets.
[10:18] Maya: any more blockers for the 3-week POC window?
[10:22] Anika: main blocker is legal/security signoff and getting the sample dataset online. We'll prioritize.
[10:29] Maya: great. recap: Redwood to send cost model, benchmark spreadsheet, security docs, POC runbook; Polaris to upload sample corpus and schedule infra deep dive.
[10:42] Jared: can you include an explicit list of encryption features and KMS options in the packet?
[10:49] Maya: yes.
[10:52] Anika: ok thanks, we will aim for upload by next wednesday.
[10:57] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and deep dive.
